The old name Sample(state, time) still does the same but is [Obsolete] and will be removed in the next version. Checking a State Use IsPlaying, HasState and Duration to check a state. Duration is the length including overrides, and 0 if there is no such state. if (anim.HasState("Open") && !anim.IsPlaying("Open")) anim.Play("Open"); Play Time Each KeyTween's Time (timeMode) decides whether playback follows Time.timeScale. Time Clock Use Scaled (default) Game time. Stops while Time.timeScale is 0 Game objects, battle effects Unscaled Real time. Keeps playing while the game is paused Pause menus, loading screens pauseMenu.timeMode = KeyTweenTimeMode.Unscaled; // applies from the next play It can be overridden per prefab instance. For example, keep a shared button Unscaled and switch only the buttons placed on the game screen to Scaled. A state played by a child call follows the child KeyTween's Time. Outside Play mode (playing from code in the editor), both use real time. When States Overlap If another playing state is animating the same property, the new state takes over only that property, from its current value. To let the earlier state reach its end pose first, call Complete before playing. anim.Complete("earlier state"); anim.Play("next state"); For details, see Guide §11. How a Play Ends The table below shows how PlayAsync ends in each case, and what happens to the events and sounds that have not been reached yet. Case PlayAsync result Callback Remaining events Remaining sounds Reaches the end completes On Complete all raised all played Complete called completes On Complete raised in order not played Another state takes all of its properties canceled On Cancel not raised not played The same state is played again earlier play canceled the earlier play's On Cancel not raised not played Object disabled canceled On Cancel not raised not played Stop called, token canceled canceled On Cancel not raised not played A play that does not reach its end ends as canceled. This makes "continue only when the play really finished" the default behavior. Start and End Callbacks You can receive the start and end of a play without await. Connect them per state in Callbacks in the editor (On Start, On Complete, On Cancel, see the Guide), or receive every state through the component's events in code. public event Action<string> StateStarted; // the state's name. After the first pose, before the events at the start time public event Action<string> StateCompleted; // reached the end, or Complete. Before PlayAsync completes public event Action<string> StateCanceled; // did not reach the end (the table above) anim.StateCompleted += state => { if (state == "Close") gameObject.SetActive(false); }; Each play starts with StateStarted and ends with exactly one of StateCompleted and StateCanceled. At the same moment, the state's UnityEvent (On Start and so on) is called first, then the component's event. A callback that throws is logged, and the play and the other callbacks go on. Stopping the state inside its On Start means the play does not start, and its PlayAsync is canceled. Stop(state, time), which writes a pose without playing, and the editor preview call no callbacks. Example: Closing a Popup If the popup is opened again while it is closing, the close play is canceled and the popup is not destroyed. try { await popup.PlayAsync("Close", cancellationToken: popup.destroyCancellationToken); } catch (OperationCanceledException) { return; } // Open took over Close's properties, so keep the popup Destroy(popup.gameObject); Example: A Dialogue Box Change the text of the same TMP object and play the same state again. To skip, call Complete. The character count is read again on each play, so the animation follows the new line. dialogue.text = nextLine; var typing = anim.PlayAsync("Typewriter"); // skip button: anim.Complete("Typewriter"); await typing; The story screen of the RPG sample shows its lines one character at a time in this way.

articles/en/preview.html.title: Preview | KeyTween
articles/en/preview.html.summary: Preview Preview lets you see how a state moves, right in the editor. Preview uses the same calculation as the runtime, so it gives the same result as real playback, including child calls and overrides. Playing a Preview Select the state to preview in the state tabs. Click ▶ in the top bar. To see the pose at a given time, drag the ruler to scrub. The following shows a preview in the editor, without entering Play mode. Loop, Speed and Sounds Loop: Turn on ⟲, or the state's Loop, to repeat. Speed: Choose from 0.1x to 1x. Sounds: Sounds that the playhead passes during playback are played. Scrubbing plays no sound. Behavior by Where You Preview Where Behavior Scene (Edit mode) The changed properties are handed to Unity's AnimationMode Prefab mode The values at the start are remembered and restored when you stop A prefab selected in the Project window The prefab opens in Prefab mode and the same state is previewed there Play mode Values are written straight to the running objects and restored when you stop In a scene, AnimationMode returns the properties to their original values when you stop, and they are not saved in the scene. When the prefab is saved in Prefab mode (Ctrl+S, or Auto Save in Unity's Prefab mode), it is saved with the original values. Then the same time is shown again. The prefab asset is not drawn in any view. Playing or scrubbing a prefab selected in the Project window therefore opens it in Prefab mode. You can also preview in Play mode with the same window. Starting Pose Chosen Automatically Some states only show their motion when they start from the pose in which another state ends. Such states are previewed from that pose. The pairs are: Play On pairs: PointerExit←PointerEnter, PointerUp←PointerDown, Deselect←Select, ToggleOff←ToggleOn Name pairs: Open↔Close, Show↔Hide, In↔Out When the Preview Stops The preview stops when you: Click ■ Change the target or the state tab Delete the state Enter or leave Play mode Reload scripts Save or close the scene Close the window

articles/en/quick-start.html.title: Quick Start | KeyTween
articles/en/quick-start.html.summary: Quick Start This section walks you through your first animation in the editor, and then shows how to play a state from code. A state is a named animation, such as Hover or Open, stored in the KeyTween component on a prefab. 1. A hover effect, in the editor In this example, the button grows to 1.1× and becomes lighter when the pointer enters it, and returns to normal when the pointer leaves. You do not write any code. When you finish, the KeyTween window shows the following: The Hover and Unhover states The button's Scale and Color tracks with their keys The key inspector on the right Open the button prefab, then open Window > KeyTween Editor. Click Add KeyTween to 'Button'. You can also add the KeyTween component yourself. Click + in the state tabs to add a state, and name it Hover in the state inspector. A new state starts with an empty timeline, and the state inspector shows its Name, Loop, Duration and Play On settings. Right-click an empty part of the timeline and choose Add Track…. Pick Scale under RectTransform and Color under Image, then click Add 2. Each track is created with a key at 0 s and an end key at 0.2 s. Click the Scale track's end key and set Value to 1.1 and Ease to OutBack. Set the Color track's end key to a lighter color. Drag the ruler or press ▶ to preview the animation. You do not need to enter Play mode. In the state inspector, set Play On to PointerEnter. Create an Unhover state the same way. Set its end keys back to 1 and the original color, and set its Play On to PointerExit. Enter Play mode and move the pointer onto the button and off it again. A full video of these steps is available: Button Hover Editor. For details on the editor, see the Guide. 2. Playing it from code To play a state from a script, reference the KeyTween component and call it with the state name. This popup plays Open when it opens, and destroys itself after Close finishes: using System; using KeyTweening; using UnityEngine; public class Popup : MonoBehaviour { [SerializeField] KeyTween anim; public async Awaitable Open() => await anim.PlayAsync("Open"); public async Awaitable Close() { try { await anim.PlayAsync("Close", cancellationToken: destroyCancellationToken); } catch (OperationCanceledException) { return; } // reopened while closing: keep the popup Destroy(gameObject); } } The editor and the code split the work as follows: The editor defines the animation itself. This includes its timing, eases and animated properties. The code only decides which state to play and what happens after it ends. For details, see Playing.

articles/en/r3.html.title: R3 | KeyTween
articles/en/r3.html.summary: R3 When R3 (com.cysharp.r3 1.0.0 or later) is installed, KeyTween gains extension methods that expose plays and animation events as observables. Method Description PlayAsObservable(stateName) Starts playing on subscribe, emits one Unit when the play ends, and completes. EventsAsObservable() Emits every animation event. EventAsObservable(eventName) Emits only the events with that name. PlayAsObservable(stateName, time), play.PlayAsObservable() Plays from that time, or a play set up with With (KeyTweenPlay). They end like PlayAsObservable(stateName). StateStartedAsObservable(), StateCompletedAsObservable(), StateCanceledAsObservable() Emit a state's name when it starts, reaches its end, or does not reach it. Installing R3 R3 needs both the Unity package and the core R3 DLL. In the Package Manager, install the Unity package from the following Git URL. https://github.com/Cysharp/R3.git?path=src/R3.Unity/Assets/R3.Unity Install the core R3 DLL from NuGet. You can use a tool such as NuGetForUnity. Observing the End of a Play PlayAsObservable emits one Unit when the play ends. Block repeated clicks with ThrottleFirst. open.OnClickAsObservable().ThrottleFirst(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(0.5)) .SelectMany(_ => popup.PlayAsObservable("Open")) .Subscribe(_ => Debug.Log("opened")).AddTo(this); If the play cannot finish, it completes with OperationCanceledException (API). Disposing the subscription stops the play where it is. Keeping Only the Last Play For a close button, use Switch to keep only the last play. close.OnClickAsObservable() .Select(_ => popup.PlayAsObservable("Close")) .Switch() .Subscribe().AddTo(this); Observing Events EventAsObservable emits only the events with that name. To receive every event, use EventsAsObservable. popup.EventAsObservable("Shown").Subscribe(e => Debug.Log(e.Time)).AddTo(this); With Plays and State Notifications A play set up with With also starts when subscribed. Disposing the subscription stops it where it is. var open = popup.With("Open").WithEase(panel, KeyTweenProperty.Scale, KeyTweenEase.OutBack); openButton.OnClickAsObservable().SelectMany(_ => open.PlayAsObservable()).Subscribe().AddTo(this); Which state started or ended comes from the state notifications, with the state's name as the value. popup.StateCompletedAsObservable() .Where(state => state == "Open") .Subscribe(_ => EnableInput()).AddTo(this);

articles/en/recording.html.title: Recording | KeyTween
articles/en/recording.html.summary: Recording With recording on, you can create keys simply by changing an object in the Scene view or the Inspector. This works the same way as recording in the Unity Animation window. Recording Keys Turn on ● in the top bar. The button turns red. Put the playhead at the time you want. Change an object in the Scene view or the Inspector. The new value becomes a key. The object itself returns to its value before the change, and the view shows the new key through preview. Each change is one Undo step. How Recording Creates Keys Case Result Properties that have a track A key is placed at the playhead. If a key already exists at that time, only its value changes Properties without a track A new track is created with a 0 s key (the value before the change) and a key at the playhead (the changed value) For Relative To Rest and Size Relative tracks, the value is converted to that basis. Recording at 0 s switches Start to Key Value so that the first key uses the recorded value. Recorded Properties A changed field is recorded onto the track that writes its value. Every track except those under "Not Recorded" is recorded (Transform, UI, TextMeshPro, SpriteRenderer, Light, Camera, AudioSource, UIEffect). If the state already has a track that writes the value, the key goes on that track. For example, with a World Position track, moving the object is recorded as World Position; with an Offset Min track, changing Position or Size is recorded as Offset Min; with a Scroll Position track, moving the Content is recorded as Scroll Position. Without such a track, the field's default track is created: Position for a position, Color for a color. If you change only the alpha of a Color and the same Graphic has an Alpha track but no Color track, the change is recorded as Alpha. With only an Alpha track, changing R, G or B creates a Color track. With a Number track, changing the number in the text is recorded as Number. Changing a text does not create a Number track. Not Recorded Material values: Material tracks and TextMeshPro's Outline Width, Outline Color, Face Dilate and Underlay Color. They change the material asset, not a field of the object. Reveal and per-character tracks Custom tracks that do not list their serialized fields. For details, see Custom Tracks. Tracks whose Start is Pointer Objects outside the KeyTween being edited in the window Saving Recorded Keys Recorded keys are saved by Auto Save and Save as well. Recording also works in Play mode, and keys recorded on a runtime copy stay in the original prefab.

articles/en/samples.html.title: Samples | KeyTween
articles/en/samples.html.summary: Samples KeyTween comes with two samples. To import one, select KeyTween in the Package Manager and open the Samples tab. Included Samples Sample What Needs RPG Sample A complete mobile RPG UI Input System UI Components Button, text effect and scroll list examples Input System RPG Sample A complete mobile RPG UI. Screens: title, lobby, heroes and upgrade, bag, summon, adventure, battle, quests, shop, mail, guild chat, ranking, story and settings Every motion is a state in a prefab. The scripts only open screens and fill in data. Scene: Scenes/RPG.unity The animations below are taken from the RPG sample: Heroes → detail (shared element) → upgrade Adventure → formation → battle → victory Ranking: a long list Mail and daily rewards UI Components Each example is in its own scene: Buttons Hover effects Toggles A popup Text effects 18 scroll list examples TextMeshPro Resources If your project does not have TMP Essential Resources (TextMeshPro's settings and shaders) yet, they are imported automatically along with the sample. Examples for UniTask and R3 are in Integrations.

articles/en/saving.html.title: Saving | KeyTween
articles/en/saving.html.summary: Saving Your edits in the KeyTween window are saved wherever that KeyTween lives. The tooltips of Auto Save and Save show where the edits are saved. Auto Save and Save Control Behavior Auto Save Saves automatically. On by default Save Saves when you click it Pressing Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on Mac) while the window has focus does the same as Save. Auto Save saves 0.4 s after your last edit, so that it does not save every frame while you drag a value. Auto Save also saves any remaining edits when Play mode ends. Undo (Ctrl+Z) is saved the same way. With Auto Save off, edits are saved only when you click Save. Where Edits Are Saved What you edit Where it is saved An object in Prefab mode That prefab A prefab asset selected in the Project window That prefab A scene object (Edit mode) The scene (with Unity's scene save) In Play mode, a prefab copy created at runtime The original prefab In Play mode, an object placed in the scene That scene object (applied when Play mode ends) When you edit a scene object in Edit mode, both controls are disabled and the tooltip explains why. Edits go straight into the object and are saved with Unity's scene save (Ctrl+S). Saving in Play Mode Prefab copies created at runtime include screens and list items. Other running copies of the same prefab get the same values immediately. Unity normally discards changes to an object placed in the scene. KeyTween applies them to that scene object when Play mode ends, and the scene file is written when you save the scene. In Play mode, edits that were not saved with Save while Auto Save was off are lost when Play mode ends. Editing part of a nested prefab in Play mode saves the change as an override in the outer prefab, and the inner prefab stays as it is. Objects in a scene that has never been saved (Untitled) cannot be found again after Play mode ends, so their edits are not applied. For overrides, see Child Calls and Overrides. Orange Dot Like the * on a scene name, the orange dot appears while the values on screen are not saved. Its tooltip says which values these are. During preview When there are unsaved edits

articles/en/screens.html.title: Screen Transitions | KeyTween
articles/en/screens.html.summary: Screen Transitions KeyTween includes components that manage the screen flow of a game UI: pages that you stack and go back from, popups (modals) shown on top, and sheets that you switch between like tabs. They do the job of UnityScreenNavigator without a separate package. A transition is a KeyTween state on the screen prefab. A state is one named animation stored on a KeyTween component. If the screen has no state with the expected name, the built-in default transition is used. Every transition returns a Unity Awaitable, so you can await it without third-party libraries. 1. Screen — KeyTweenScreen KeyTweenScreen represents one screen that can be a page, a modal or a sheet. Making a Screen Prefab Select the root of the screen prefab. Choose Add Component > KeyTween > Screen. The same object also needs these components: RectTransform CanvasGroup KeyTween A screen created by a container fills the container. Drawing Order — renderingOrder In a page container, a page with a higher value draws on top. Pages with equal values stack in the order they were added. In a modal container the modal opened last is on top; in a sheet container, the sheet passed to Show last. Transitioning Without Animation A transition with animated: false skips the animation and jumps straight to the state's end pose. Use it when nobody needs to see the transition, such as when the game starts or a saved screen is restored. await pages.Push(homePrefab, animated: false); // the first screen, without the slide The state is not played then, only its end pose is written, so the transition state's On Start and On Complete are not called. The lifecycle methods (WillEnter, DidEnter and so on) are called as usual. Callbacks of Transition States A transition plays its state with PlayAsync, so the transition state's On Start and On Complete are called. If a transition state does not reach its end (its On Start calls Stop, or another state takes the same properties), Push, Pop and Show throw OperationCanceledException. The screens are then left in a middle pose and the lifecycle's Did... methods are not called. Do not stop a transition state during a transition. 2. Containers Screens are created and managed by a container. There are three kinds of container, and each looks for different state names on the screen and has its own default transition. Container Screens Default transition (0.3 s) KeyTweenPageContainer Pages you stack and go back from Slide by one screen width (Size Relative), OutQuart KeyTweenModalContainer Modals shown on top Scale 0.3 → 1 with alpha (OutQuart); the backdrop fades its alpha (Linear) KeyTweenSheetContainer Sheets you switch between Alpha fade (Linear) Adding a Container Inside the Canvas, make the object that will be the screens' area, usually a RectTransform that fills the Canvas. Choose Add Component > KeyTween > Page Container (or Modal Container, Sheet Container). A CanvasGroup is added with it. In code, open screens by handing screen prefabs to this container. [SerializeField] KeyTweenPageContainer pages; [SerializeField] KeyTweenScreen shopPrefab; public async void OpenShop() => await pages.Push(shopPrefab); A screen the container makes is fitted to fill the container's area. To use pages and modals together, make two containers and put the modal container lower in the Hierarchy (the side drawn on top). Pages — KeyTweenPageContainer API: Push(prefab, animated, stack), Pop(animated), Pages, Current State names: PushEnter, PushExit, PopEnter, PopExit await pages.Push(loadingPage, stack: false); // loading screen: removed from history and destroyed when the next page comes in await pages.Push(homePage); // the loading screen stays visible while Home prepares in WillEnter Push runs in this order: It creates the new page. It waits for the Will* methods of both the incoming and the outgoing page. It plays PushEnter and PushExit at the same time. It deactivates the outgoing page when they finish. A page pushed with stack: false is removed from history and destroyed when the next page comes in. Use it for a loading screen. Pop reactivates the previous page, plays PopEnter and PopExit, and then destroys the current page. Pop does nothing if there is no page. The RPG sample uses Push to go from the lobby to a hero's detail page and from there to the upgrade page, and Pop to come back. Modals — KeyTweenModalContainer API: Push(prefab, animated), Pop(animated), Modals, Current, backdropPrefab State names: Enter, Exit (the backdrop also uses Enter/Exit) await modals.Push(confirmPopup); await modals.Pop(); Each modal gets its own backdrop. If backdropPrefab is empty, a black backdrop at 75% opacity is created. Modals underneath do not move, and their lifecycle methods are not called. Pop plays Exit, then destroys the modal and its backdrop. The Daily Attendance window in the RPG sample is opened with the modal container. While the window comes in, the backdrop darkens the lobby behind it. Sheets — KeyTweenSheetContainer API: Register(prefab), Show(index, animated), Sheets, ActiveIndex, Active State names: Enter, Exit State names when going to a lower index: EnterBackward, ExitBackward (Enter/Exit if missing) var tab = sheets.Register(shopTabPrefab); await sheets.Show(tab); // to a higher index: Enter, to a lower index: EnterBackward Register creates a sheet, keeps it hidden and returns its index. Show does nothing when given the current index or an index out of range. The outgoing sheet is deactivated. Default Transition Values The default values match UnityScreenNavigator's defaults. You can also use them directly in code through KeyTweenDefaultTransitions: PagePushEnter and so on Slide FadeIn / FadeOut Each is a function that takes a KeyTweenScreen and returns a new KeyTweenState. Name it and add it with AddState, and it plays like any other state. var fade = KeyTweenDefaultTransitions.FadeIn(screen); fade.name = "FadeIn"; screen.Animation.AddState(fade); 3. Input Blocking While a transition is running, touch input is blocked on every container, so rapid taps cannot start overlapping transitions. Checking for a Running Transition KeyTweenScreenContainer.AnyInTransition tells whether any container is in a transition. IsInTransition tells whether a particular container is in a transition. How Input Is Blocked Input is blocked through each container's CanvasGroup.blocksRaycasts. interactable is left unchanged, so buttons do not switch to their disabled color during a transition. A container object needs a RectTransform and a CanvasGroup. 4. Lifecycle — IKeyTweenScreenLifecycle Use this interface to run code when a screen enters or exits. Implementing Lifecycle Methods If any component on the screen root implements it, its methods are called on every transition. Every method has a default implementation, so you only write the ones you need. public sealed class HomePage : MonoBehaviour, IKeyTweenScreenLifecycle { public async Awaitable WillEnter(KeyTweenTransition t) { await LoadAsync(); } // called before the animation and awaited public void DidEnter(KeyTweenTransition t) { } // after the animation public Awaitable WillExit(KeyTweenTransition t) => KeyTweenScreen.Completed(); // when there is nothing to await public void DidExit(KeyTweenTransition t) { } } Transition Info — KeyTweenTransition The KeyTweenTransition passed to each method has the following properties. Property Description Kind The kind of transition: Push, Pop, Show or Hide Partner The other screen in the transition Backward Whether the transition goes backward Animated Whether the transition plays its animation Backward is true for these transitions: Pop for pages and modals A move to a lower index for sheets 5. Shared Element Transition — KeyTweenSharedElement A shared element transition connects two screens through one element. For example, a portrait in a list moves into the portrait's place on the detail screen and grows as it goes. Making a Shared Element Transition You make the motion in the editor, and fill in the place on the other screen, which is known only at runtime, from code. Add a Position track and a Size track to the moving image and set keys on them. In a Will* method, fill in only the key for the place on the other screen (the first key or the last key). // RPG sample RpgHeroDetail: the hero card's portrait (card) moves into the detail screen's portrait (portrait) public Awaitable WillEnter(KeyTweenTransition t) { KeyTweenSharedElement.SetPartnerKeys(GetComponent<KeyTween>(), "PushEnter", portrait.rectTransform, card, atStart: true); card.GetComponent<Image>().enabled = false; // hide the card's image; show it again after returning from the detail screen return KeyTweenScreen.Completed(); } public Awaitable WillExit(KeyTweenTransition t) { if (t.Kind == KeyTweenTransitionKind.Pop) // going back: the last key goes to the card's place KeyTweenSharedElement.SetPartnerKeys(GetComponent<KeyTween>(), "PopExit", portrait.rectTransform, card, atStart: false); return KeyTweenScreen.Completed(); } SetPartnerKeys SetPartnerKeys(animation, state, moving, partner, atStart) converts the rectangle that partner occupies on screen into a position and size for moving. It writes them to keys of the Position and Size tracks. With atStart true it writes the first key, otherwise the last key. It assumes that moving has point anchors (not stretch). Examples The hero card to detail screen transition in the RPG sample The bag slot to item info popup transition The portrait viewer in the ScreenNavigator recreation In the bag of the RPG sample, tapping a slot carries the item icon into its place in the item info popup.

articles/en/scroll-list.html.title: Scroll List | KeyTween
articles/en/scroll-list.html.summary: Scroll List KeyTweenScrollList is the component for UI that scrolls through many entries, such as rankings, quest lists, chats, carousels and banners. It is a virtualized list that you add to a ScrollRect. Only the visible items exist as objects, and those objects are reused as you scroll, so the object count stays at what fits on screen even with hundreds of entries. There is no separate component for each scroll style. Vertical lists, grids, carousels, wheel pickers and the other styles are all combinations of this list's settings. Every animation is a KeyTween state on the item (or on a page dot or section header). A state is one named animation stored on a KeyTween component. To add it, select the object that has the ScrollRect and choose Add Component > KeyTween > Scroll List. 1. Items and Layout This section explains how to set the item prefabs and the layout. The list's inspector is organized like a Unity Layout Group. Setting the Item Prefabs Item Description Item Prefab The default item prefab (number 0). Its size is the default item size. Extra Prefabs Additional prefabs for lists with several kinds of items (numbered from 1) Measure Items Measures each item from its layout preferred size. Layout One of Vertical, Horizontal, Grid and Masonry You pick the kind from Extra Prefabs in code with prefabOf(index). Each kind is pooled separately. Use Measure Items for a chat bubble that grows with long text. Choosing a Layout Each layout has the following settings. Layout Settings Vertical / Horizontal Padding, Spacing, Child Alignment, Reverse Arrangement, Control Child Size Grid Padding, Cell Size, Spacing, Child Alignment, Constraint, Constraint Count Masonry Same as Grid, but with Column Size (column width) instead of Cell Size Control Child Size takes Width or Height and stretches items across the scroll direction. Grid's Constraint is one of Flexible, Fixed Column Count and Fixed Row Count. Masonry places each item on the shortest column. Scroll Direction and Item Size The layout determines the scroll direction. A Grid with Fixed Row Count scrolls horizontally. The item size along the scroll direction comes from the following, in order. Grid always uses Cell Size. The sizeOf(index) callback Measure Items The prefab size When the content is shorter than the viewport, Child Alignment also applies along the scroll direction. A chat, for example, uses Lower so that messages stack from the bottom. Layout Cost Item positions are computed once whenever the layout changes, without a LayoutGroup. The list costs nothing while it is not scrolling. 2. Binding Data This section explains how to connect data to the list. You bind data with callbacks, as with UI Toolkit's ListView. Binding with Callbacks The item prefab does not need a base class. ItemView in the code below stands for any component on the prefab. list.SetCount(100, (ItemView view, int index) => view.Set(items[index]), (ItemView view, int index) => view.Clear()); // unbind is optional list.SetData(items, (ItemView view, Item item, int index) => view.Set(item)); The binding callback is called only when an item becomes visible. Calling SetCount or SetData with bindings refills the list from scratch. A refill returns the scroll position to the start, or to the end when Stick To End is on. With Play On Fill, the entry animation also plays. Using Several Prefab Kinds With several prefab kinds, take a RectTransform and pick the kind for each index with prefabOf. list.prefabOf = i => items[i].isHeader ? 1 : 0; // set before SetCount list.SetCount(48, (RectTransform item, int index) => ...); // with several prefabs Changing the Count and Rebinding Changing only the count, without bindings, keeps the scroll position. The remaining items keep their objects and are bound again, without playing Appear again. list.SetCount(10); // count only: keeps the scroll position, rebinds the remaining items, only newly visible ones Appear list.Refresh(); // rebinds every visible item (and re-measures with Measure Items) list.RefreshItem(5); SetCount(count, stickDuration = 0.25f), which changes only the count, measures only the new items. If Stick To End is on and the end was in view, the list slides to the new end over stickDuration seconds. Example: Guild Chat The guild chat in the RPG sample only raises the count when a message arrives. Each bubble is sized to its text (Measure Items). The list keeps the newest message in view (Stick To End). 3. Position and Scrolling This section explains how to read the list's current state, move to a specific item and set how the list scrolls. Reading the State API Description Count The item count VisibleRange The visible range Offset The pixels scrolled from the start AtEnd Whether the list is at the end ItemSize The default item size GetItem(index), GetItem<TView>(index) The item's object if it is visible, otherwise null IndexAt(screenPoint, camera) The index of the item under a screen point (such as the pointer), or −1 ItemPosition(index), SizeOf(index) An item's position and size NearestIndex(alignment) The item nearest to an alignment point CurrentIndex, CurrentIndexChanged The item at the Snap Alignment point ItemShown Raised when an item becomes visible (after binding) ItemHidden Raised when an item is hidden (before unbinding) Use CurrentIndex for the current page or the selection of a carousel or wheel picker. Scrolling to an Item ScrollTo(index, alignment = Start, duration = 0) aligns the item to the start, center or end of the viewport. The move uses OutCubic. A duration of 0 jumps instantly. With Loop, it goes the shorter way. Folding and Removing Items ResizeItem(index, size, duration) animates one item's size while the items after it follow (accordion). Call RemoveItem(index) after removing one entry from your data. await list.ResizeItem(index, 0f, foldSeconds); // fold; the Awaitable completes when the animation ends items.RemoveAt(index); // remove the entry from your data list.RemoveItem(index); // only that item goes away After RemoveItem, the items below move up one slot. They keep their objects and animation state. They are not rebound and do not play the appear animation. Replaying and Rebuilding PlayEntry() replays the entry animation. Rebuild() recomputes the layout. Scrolling Settings Setting Description Loop The first item follows the last one. Snap: None No snapping. Snap: Nearest Snaps to the nearest item on release. Snap: One Per Swipe Moves exactly one item per drag. Snap Alignment / Duration Where items snap to / how long the snap takes Auto Scroll (s) Moves to the next item every N seconds (banner). Stick To End When items are added while the end is in view, the list stays at the end (chat). Sticky Header Uses the chosen prefab kind as a section header. Loop and Sticky Header work with Vertical and Horizontal only. With One Per Swipe, a drag under 30 px returns to where it was. Auto Scroll pauses while the user drags. With Sticky Header, a header that has scrolled past stays pinned at the top until the next header pushes it up. Nested Scrolling A drag across the list's scroll axis is passed to the enclosing ScrollRect. This is how these layouts behave: A vertical list inside a page A horizontal row inside a vertical list Example: Quest List The quest list in the RPG sample pins its section headers with Sticky Header. Section headers: DAILY, WEEKLY, ACHIEVEMENTS A row whose reward has been claimed is folded with ResizeItem and then removed with RemoveItem. 4. Item Animation This section explains the animations items play when they come in and as they scroll. You pick the states from the item prefab's KeyTween. Editing States The buttons on each state row let you edit a state right away. Edit opens that state in the KeyTween Editor. Create adds the KeyTween and the state if they are missing, then opens it. For a prefab asset, Prefab Mode opens first. Entry Animation — Entry State Entry State works together with Stagger and Play On Fill. On the first fill (or when you call PlayEntry()), the visible items play one after another, Stagger apart. Items still waiting for their turn show the state's start pose. Items that come in after the entry animation has finished show its end pose. Appear Animation — Appear State Plays on an item that becomes visible by scrolling. It does not play in these cases: On the first fill On items that come into view because another item was resized or removed A reused object may still look like its previous index. So when an item becomes visible, the list first sets it to the entry state's end pose and then plays the appear state. Position-Driven Animation — Scrub State Uses the item's position in the viewport as the state time and applies the pose at that time (Stop(state, time)). 0 = start edge 0.5 = center 1 = end These values are fractions of the state's length, so put the keys at 0 s, half the state's length and its full length. For example, a carousel whose center item grows, with a state 1 s long, has Scale keys at 0 s = 0.8, 0.5 s = 1.1 and 1 s = 0.8. Use it for carousel zoom, wheel picker tilt and page parallax. Callbacks Entry and Appear are plays, so their states' On Start and On Complete are called. If an item leaves the view while playing and its object is reused, On Cancel is called. Scrub only sets the pose without playing, so it calls no callbacks. Example: Ranking List Rows come in one after another when the page opens. Rows that scroll into view play the appear animation. The MY RANK button uses ScrollTo to move to the player's row. 5. Editor Preview The Preview section of the inspector lets you check the list without entering Play Mode. Using the Preview It is available in Edit Mode when an Item Prefab is set. Show / Update lays out the number of items set in Items (1–200). The Scroll slider changes the scroll position, including the effect of scrub states. Play Entry plays the entry animation. Clear removes the temporary objects. The laid-out items are temporary objects that are not saved. 6. Helper Components This section covers three components that work together with the list. Their animations are also KeyTween states, and the Edit / Create buttons on their state fields open the KeyTween Editor directly. Component Use States KeyTweenPageIndicator Page dots, banner dots, tab bars On / Off KeyTweenScrollScrub A header that collapses as you scroll Any one state KeyTweenPullToRefresh Pull to refresh Pull / Refreshing Page Dots and Tab Bars — KeyTweenPageIndicator It creates one indicator item from its prefab for each list item. This object's Layout Group lays them out. Pressing an indicator item's Button scrolls the list to that item. Set tab text with labels. Collapsing Header — KeyTweenScrollScrub Uses the scroll distance (0 to Distance px) as the state time. At 0 px the state is at its start; scrolled by Distance, it shows its end pose. Use it for a header that collapses or a toolbar that appears as the list scrolls. Add Add Component > KeyTween > Scroll Scrub to any object. Put the list in List, the header's KeyTween in Target and the name of the collapsing state in State. Set Distance to the scroll distance (px) at which it is fully collapsed. Pull to Refresh — KeyTweenPullToRefresh Add it to the same object as the list. It works with vertical lists only. When you pull past the start, the Pull state follows how far you pull. Releasing past Distance calls onRefresh. While refreshing, it loops the Refreshing state and keeps the top open (Refreshing = true). Calling EndRefresh() closes it. pull.onRefresh.AddListener(async () => { var items = await LoadItemsAsync(); list.SetData(items, (ItemView view, Item item, int index) => view.Bind(item)); pull.EndRefresh(); }); 7. What You Can Build This section lists the patterns you can build from the list's settings and states. Opening the Example Scene The UI Components sample (Package Manager > KeyTween > Samples) contains 18 examples in Scenes/Scroll.unity. Settings for Each Pattern Pattern Settings / States Vertical list, horizontal list, grid, horizontal grid Layout, Entry Show + Appear Appear Carousel Scrub Focus (zooms the center item), Snap Nearest Center Paging One Per Swipe, Scrub Parallax, Page Indicator Infinite loop Loop + Scrub + Snap Auto banner Loop + One Per Swipe + Auto Scroll + Page Indicator Wheel picker Scrub Wheel (Rotation X, alpha, scale), Snap Nearest Center Section headers Two prefab kinds, Sticky Header Variable size, chat Measure Items (+ Stick To End, Lower alignment) Accordion Open/Close states + ResizeItem Masonry Masonry Nested scroll A horizontal list in each row of a vertical list Tabs Page Indicator (On/Off underline) + One Per Swipe Collapsing header Scroll Scrub Pull to refresh Pull To Refresh

articles/en/shortcuts.html.title: Context Menus and Shortcuts | KeyTween
articles/en/shortcuts.html.summary: Context Menus and Shortcuts These are the context menus and keyboard shortcuts available in the KeyTween window. Context Menus Where Menu State tab Rename, Duplicate, Move Left, Move Right, Delete Empty part of the timeline Paste Keys at Playhead, Paste Keys Here, Add Track..., Add Child Call ▸ child ▸ state Keyframe track header Add Key at Playhead, Remove Track (on an override track: Revert Track to Original) Keyframe row Add Key Here, Copy Selected Keys, Paste Keys at Playhead, Paste Keys Here, Delete Selected Keys, Remove Track Event or sound track header Add Event / Sound at Playhead, Remove Track Event or sound marker Delete Child call Revert All (outermost overrides), Remove Child Call Shortcuts Key Action Ctrl+S (Cmd+S) Save Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V (Cmd+C / Cmd+V) Copies the selected keys / pastes them at the playhead Delete / Backspace Deletes the selected keys and markers F Frame all Esc Closes the context menu When you are editing a scene object in Edit mode, Ctrl+S runs Unity's scene save instead. You can change the Save shortcut at KeyTween/Save in Edit > Shortcuts. Every edit can be undone with Unity's Undo.

articles/en/states.html.title: States | KeyTween
articles/en/states.html.summary: States A state is one named animation. You create a state for each situation, such as Hover, Open or Close, and play it from code or through Play On. Adding a State Click + in the state tabs. States are named State, State 1, and so on. Select the new state's tab. The timeline is empty and the state inspector appears. Working with State Tabs To Do this Rename Double-click the tab, type the new name and press Enter. Esc cancels Duplicate Right-click the tab › Duplicate. The copy appears right after it as Name Copy and opens Reorder Drag the tab sideways and drop it. Right-click › Move Left / Move Right also works Delete Right-click the tab › Delete (after you confirm) You can also rename with right-click › Rename or Name in the state inspector. Play On links follow a new name. An empty name, or a name another state already uses, is not accepted, because code and Play On find states by name. A duplicated state does not get a copy of Play On: one event plays one state. State Inspector When no track or key is selected, the inspector shows the state's settings. Item Contents Name The state's name. Play On links follow a new name Loop When playback reaches the end, it continues seamlessly from 0 s and repeats Duration The state's length and track count (for example, Duration 0.80s · 3 track(s)) Play On None or an event Callbacks Functions to call when a play starts (On Start), reaches its end (On Complete), or does not reach its end (On Cancel) Delete State Deletes the state after you confirm Loop is the same idea as Loop Time on an Animator clip. Events, sounds and child calls fire again on every loop. Choosing an event in Play On adds a KeyTweenTrigger component automatically. For the available events, see Play On. Calling Functions at the Start and End (Callbacks) In Callbacks in the state settings, connect functions to call when a play starts and ends. It works like a Button's OnClick: drag in an object and choose a function. Each state has its own. Field When it is called On Start When a play starts (any play method: Play, PlayAsync, PlayReversed, With(...).Play and so on). After the first pose, before the animation events at the start time On Complete When the play reaches its end, or Complete skips there. After the animation events at the end, before PlayAsync completes On Cancel When the play does not reach its end: Stop, another state took everything it animates, the object was disabled, the same state was played again, or the PlayAsync token was canceled Each play starts with On Start and ends with exactly one of On Complete and On Cancel. A looping state calls On Start once at the beginning, and On Complete only when you call Complete. Stop(state, time), which writes a pose without playing, calls no callbacks. Stopping a playing state with it calls On Cancel. The preview in this window does not call callbacks, so that no game code runs while you preview. Callbacks are saved in the prefab, and a prefab instance can override them like any other Unity value. In code, the StateStarted, StateCompleted and StateCanceled events report every state in one place. For details, see API. State Length A state's length is set by whatever ends last. The latest of the following is the state's length: The last key of a track An event The end of a sound The end of a child call

articles/en/text-tracks.html.title: Text Tracks | KeyTween
articles/en/text-tracks.html.summary: Text Tracks Text tracks animate the characters of a TMP_Text. You can reveal characters one after another, count a number, or move each character on its own. They are used for things like these: A typewriter in a dialogue box, one character at a time: Reveal Gold counting up from 0 on a reward screen: Number A title whose letters hop up one after another in a wave: per-character Position, Scale Open the card of an object with a TMP_Text in the Add Track window to find these tracks. In code: to count to a different number each time, give the end value with With. To skip the typewriter on a click, call Complete. anim.With("Count").WithEndValue(goldText, KeyTweenProperty.TextNumber, gold).Play(); anim.Complete("Type"); // shows the whole line at once Reveal (Typewriter) Sets how many characters are visible, as a ratio from 0 to 1. Rich text tags are not counted as characters. Scramble fills the characters that are not shown yet with random characters. Spaces in the original text are kept, so line breaks do not jump. Choose the character set from: Uppercase Lowercase Numerals All Number (Count) Counts and changes only the first number in the text, and leaves the other characters as they are. Examples: 21/100, Lv. 3 Supports integers and thousands separators (1,234). With Start set to Current Value, counting starts from the number currently shown. To set the end number at runtime, play the state with With(state).WithEndValue(...) from code (SetEndValue for a state that something else plays). The last key's value in the window then becomes a value for preview only. For details, see API. Per-Character Tracks Char Scale, Char Position, Char Rotation, Char Color and Char Alpha are per-character tracks. Their keys describe the motion of a single character. Option Meaning Stagger (s) The i-th character starts i × stagger seconds later Duration per Char (s) When greater than 0, the i-th character plays all of its keys over i × this value, in seconds On the timeline, the faint tail after the last key is the span in which the later characters play. Drag the end of the tail to change Stagger. Combining Per-Character Tracks When the same text has several per-character tracks, their results are combined. Property Combined by Scale Multiplying Position, rotation Adding Color, alpha Overwriting Playing After Changing the Text A state with text tracks reads the character count again when it plays. If you change the text and then play the state, the length and spacing follow the new text.

articles/en/track-options.html.title: Track Options | KeyTween
articles/en/track-options.html.summary: Track Options Track options decide where the first key's value comes from and what the key values are measured against. Select a track to see them in the track inspector. Start Sets where the first key's value comes from. The problem this option deals with is a play that is cut short. Say a button is growing from 1 to 1.08 and the mouse leaves halfway (at 1.04), so Unhover plays. If Unhover's first key is the written value (1.08), the size jumps from 1.04 to 1.08 and then shrinks. If the first key is the value at the moment the play starts (1.04), the motion carries on from there. Value Meaning Key Value The value written in the key Current Value The value at the moment playback starts Pointer (press position) Where the pointer that played the state was pressed. Only on the Position track of a UI object (RectTransform), and only when Play On is a pointer event With Current Value, the value does not jump even when playback is cut short. This suits hover and unhover, or open and close. Use Key Value when the motion must start from the same place every time, such as an entrance that starts from 0. If the first key of a Current Value track is placed after 0 s, the track waits that long before it starts moving. With Pointer, the later keys are relative to the press point, so (0,0) means "the spot that was pressed". Use it for button ripples. Relative To Rest Adds the key values to the original value. An example is one "shrink a little when pressed" motion used on buttons of different sizes. Writing a value such as (200, 80) in a Size track fits only a button of that size. With Relative To Rest on and −(34, 17) written, every button shrinks by 34×17 from its own size. The original value is: At runtime: the value at Awake In preview: the value when the preview starts Size Relative Key values are read as multiples of the target's own size, so x = 1 means its own width. This option is for the Position and Size tracks of a UI object (RectTransform) only. The motion therefore keeps the same proportions at any resolution. For example, a screen can slide in from one screen width to the right (x = 1) to 0. Options on Text Tracks The options above belong to keyframe tracks. Text tracks have different options. A Reveal track has only Scramble. Per-character tracks have only Stagger and Duration per Char. The Start of Reveal and per-character tracks is always Key Value. A Number track has Start and Relative To Rest like any other track. For details, see Text Tracks.

articles/en/uieffect.html.title: UIEffect | KeyTween
articles/en/uieffect.html.summary: UIEffect When UIEffect (com.coffee.ui-effect 5.x) is installed, the Add Track window shows 14 UIEffect tracks for any object that has UIEffect. The tracks are named UIEffect · … and match the Timeline tracks that UIEffect provides. Added Tracks Track Range Tone Intensity, Color Intensity, Sampling Intensity, Transition Rate (dissolve etc.), Edge Shiny Rate, Gradation Intensity, Detail Intensity 0 ~ 1 Gradation Offset −1 ~ 1 Gradation Rotation 0 ~ 360 Gradation Scale 0.01 ~ 10 Color, Transition Color, Edge Color, Detail Color color Editing the Tracks Like any other track, these tracks support the following. Keys Eases Start (Current etc.) Preview Reversed play Looping Number tracks are edited with a slider for their range, and color tracks with a color field. If UIEffect Is Removed If UIEffect is removed, these tracks no longer appear in the list. Tracks that were already saved do nothing, and no errors occur. How the Integration Works The core assembly does not reference UIEffect. KeyTweenProperty holds only the property names. The integration assembly registers reading, writing and ranges with KeyTweenExternalProperties.Register. Other libraries can be integrated the same way. For details, see Design.

articles/en/unitask.html.title: UniTask | KeyTween
articles/en/unitask.html.summary: UniTask The KeyTween package works without any third-party library. When one of the libraries below is installed in the project, its integration code compiles automatically. When it is not installed, the integration code is left out of the build, and there is nothing to configure. This is the same approach that LitMotion and VContainer take for their UniTask integrations. Library Turned on when (asmdef versionDefines) Adds UniTask com.cysharp.unitask 2.0.0 or later → KEYTWEEN_UNITASK Extension methods (plays and events as UniTasks) R3 com.cysharp.r3 1.0.0 or later → KEYTWEEN_R3 Extension methods (plays, events and state notifications as observables) UIEffect com.coffee.ui-effect 5.0.0 or later → KEYTWEEN_UIEFFECT 14 tracks (assembly KeyTween.UIEffect) When UniTask (com.cysharp.unitask 2.0.0 or later) is installed, KeyTween gains extension methods for awaiting plays and events as UniTasks. Method Description PlayUniTaskAsync(stateName, ct) The UniTask version of PlayAsync. PlayUniTaskAsync(stateName, time, ct) Plays from that time (in seconds). PlayReversedUniTaskAsync(stateName, ct), (stateName, time, ct) Plays the state reversed. play.PlayUniTaskAsync(ct), play.PlayReversedUniTaskAsync(ct) Awaits a play set up with With (KeyTweenPlay) as a UniTask. WaitEventUniTaskAsync(eventName, ct) Waits until the next animation event is raised. Awaiting Several Plays Together When opening a popup, use WhenAll to play the popup and its backdrop together. await UniTask.WhenAll(popup.PlayUniTaskAsync("Open"), dim.PlayUniTaskAsync("Show")); The completion and cancellation rules are the same as for PlayAsync (API). Internally, the Awaitable is converted with AsUniTask(). Receiving a Cancel as a Value When closing a popup, use SuppressCancellationThrow to receive a cancel as a value instead of an exception. var canceled = await popup.PlayUniTaskAsync("Close").SuppressCancellationThrow(); Setting a Time Limit For a slow state, apply Timeout, then call Complete when the time runs out. try { await anim.PlayUniTaskAsync("Intro").Timeout(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(3)); } catch (TimeoutException) { anim.Complete("Intro"); } Waiting for an Event Use WaitEventUniTaskAsync to wait for an animation event. var info = await anim.WaitEventUniTaskAsync("Shown"); Cleaning Up with the Object In every case, pass destroyCancellationToken so that the work is cleaned up when the object is destroyed. await popup.PlayUniTaskAsync("Open", destroyCancellationToken); From a Given Time, With, Build Plays from a given time and plays set up with With are awaited as UniTasks too. For a state made with Build, carry on with .With(). await anim.PlayUniTaskAsync("Intro", 1.5f, destroyCancellationToken); // from 1.5 s await popup.With("Open").WithEase(panel, KeyTweenProperty.Scale, KeyTweenEase.OutBack).PlayUniTaskAsync(destroyCancellationToken); await anim.Build("Pop").Track(icon.transform, KeyTweenProperty.Scale).Key(0f, Vector3.zero).Key(0.2f, Vector3.one).With().PlayUniTaskAsync();

articles/en/values.html.title: Reading and Writing Values | KeyTween
articles/en/values.html.summary: Reading and Writing Values You can read and write a single property that a track animates directly from code, without playing anything. Reading and Writing a Property KeyTween.Read and KeyTween.Write are static methods. public static Vector4 KeyTween.Read(Component target, KeyTweenProperty property); public static void KeyTween.Write(Component target, KeyTweenProperty property, Vector4 value); They handle the different Unity APIs behind each property (Image.color, RectTransform.anchoredPosition, the number in a text and so on) in one form. For example, to put back a saved value, or to read the same value a track would in a custom tool. Vector4 color = KeyTween.Read(image, KeyTweenProperty.GraphicColor); KeyTween.Write(label, KeyTweenProperty.TextNumber, new Vector4(1234, 0, 0, 0)); // "1,234" How Values Are Interpreted Values are interpreted the same way tracks interpret them. Properties with a single value use x. Rotation is read in the range −180..180. TextNumber reads the first integer in the text and writes in 1,234 format. Per-character properties cannot be written, because they are applied directly to the mesh while playing.

articles/en/with.html.title: Setting Up a Play in Code | KeyTween
articles/en/with.html.summary: Setting Up a Play in Code Make the motion in the editor, and set in code only what changes from play to play: the target number of a currency or power rating, a different arrival for the situation, what to do when it finishes. Set up a play with With(state), then play it with one of the Play methods. The calls chain like LitMotion's WithEase. // "Count" state on the gold label: a Number (Count) track, Start = Current Value, 0.6 s OutQuad (made in the editor) count.With("Count").WithEndValue(goldLabel, KeyTweenProperty.TextNumber, gold).Play(); // Opening a popup: arrive with OutBack this time, and take input once it is open await popup.With("Open") .WithEase(panel, KeyTweenProperty.Scale, KeyTweenEase.OutBack) .WithOnComplete(EnableInput) .PlayAsync(destroyCancellationToken); What You Can Change The track is found by state name, target and property, and what changes is its last key (the end value and the segment that arrives there). Method Changes WithEndValue(target, property, value) The last key's value. The float overload is for built-in properties and sets x only WithEase(target, property, ease) The last key's arrival becomes Ease, with that ease WithCurve(target, property, curve) The arrival becomes Curve, with that AnimationCurve WithPunch(target, property, frequency = 10, damping = 1), WithShake(...) The arrival becomes Punch / Shake, with those values. The strength stays the value written in the key WithTime(time) Plays from that time in seconds (the same as Play(state, time)) WithEventsBefore(raise = true) With WithTime: the animation events before that time are raised too, in order, at the start (sounds and child calls are skipped) WithOnStart, WithOnComplete, WithOnCancel Callbacks for this play only, called after the state's On Start and so on WithOnLoop For a looping state, each time a lap ends A Material track is found by its shader property name, as in WithEase(renderer, "_BaseColor", ease), and a custom track by its class, as in WithEase<MyTrack>(target, ease). A value is interpreted exactly like a key value, so the Relative To Rest and Size Relative settings apply. If no track matches, it logs a warning and skips that change. The state still plays. With has no play that takes a PointerEventData. Play a state with a Start = Pointer track with Play(state, eventData). WithTime, WithEventsBefore and WithOnLoop are used like this: // Loading a saved game: carry on from 0.8 s, and get the events before it ("DoorOpened" and so on) in order to catch up door.With("Open").WithTime(0.8f).WithEventsBefore().Play(); // Count the laps of a looping state int laps = 0; wheel.With("Spin").WithOnLoop(() => laps++).Play(); For That Play Only The changes go in when the play starts and are put back when it ends, whether it completes or is canceled. The next Play uses the values set in the editor. The saved data is not changed. You can keep what With returns and play it again as often as you like. Reused, it does not allocate when it plays. KeyTweenPlay _open; void Awake() => _open = popup.With("Open").WithEase(panel, KeyTweenProperty.Scale, KeyTweenEase.OutBack); public void Show() => _open.Play(); End Values for States Played Elsewhere You cannot use With for a state that something other than your code plays, such as Play On or a screen transition. Set its end value beforehand with SetEndValue instead. The value then applies to every later play. public void SetEndValue(string stateName, Component target, KeyTweenProperty property, Vector4 value); public void SetEndValue(string stateName, Component target, KeyTweenProperty property, float value); // sets x only SetEndValue finds built-in property tracks only. Change the end value of a Material or custom track with With. // Result screen: when the screen transition plays "Enter", the gold counts up to this number result.SetEndValue("Enter", goldLabel, KeyTweenProperty.TextNumber, reward);

articles/ko/adding-tracks.html.title: 트랙 추가 | KeyTween
articles/ko/adding-tracks.html.summary: 트랙 추가 트랙은 오브젝트 하나의 속성 하나를 움직입니다. 트랙은 트랙 추가 창에서 골라 상태에 넣습니다. 트랙 추가 창 열기 타임라인의 빈 곳을 우클릭하고 Add Track... 항목을 고릅니다. 트랙 고르기 트랙 추가 창의 왼쪽에는 Prefab 안의 오브젝트 트리가 있고, 오른쪽에는 선택한 오브젝트에서 만들 수 있는 트랙 카드가 현재 값과 함께 나옵니다. 왼쪽 트리에서 오브젝트를 고릅니다. 트리는 검색할 수 있습니다. 오른쪽에서 트랙 카드를 클릭해 고릅니다. 여러 개를 고를 수 있습니다. Add N을 누릅니다. 카드를 더블클릭하면 바로 추가됩니다. 다른 오브젝트로 옮겨 가며 골라도 선택은 유지됩니다. 이미 있는 트랙에는 Added 표시가 붙습니다. 새 트랙의 기본값 0초 키와 상태 끝 시간의 키가 생깁니다. 두 키 모두 지금 값을 가집니다. 상태가 비어 있으면 끝 키는 0.2초에 생깁니다. Start는 Current Value입니다. Reveal과 글자별 트랙만 Key Value로 생깁니다. 끝 키의 도착 방식은 Ease OutSine입니다. 글자별 트랙의 Stagger는 0.05초입니다. Start 옵션은 트랙 옵션을 참고하세요. 만들 수 있는 트랙 트랙 추가 창은 고른 오브젝트에 붙은 컴포넌트에 맞는 트랙만 보여 줍니다. 오브젝트 대상 트랙 모든 오브젝트 Scale, Rotation, Active UI가 아닌 오브젝트 (Transform) Position, World Position, World Rotation UI 대상 트랙 RectTransform Position, Size, Anchor Min, Anchor Max, Pivot, Offset Min, Offset Max CanvasGroup Group Alpha Graphic (Image, RawImage, TMP 등) Color, Alpha Image (Image Type = Filled) Fill Amount RawImage UV Rect Shadow, Outline Effect Color, Effect Distance RectMask2D Softness, Padding Slider Value ScrollRect Scroll Position LayoutElement Min Size, Preferred Size, Flexible Size TextMeshPro 대상 트랙 TMP_Text Font Size, Character Spacing, Word Spacing, Line Spacing, Reveal (Typewriter), Number (Count) TMP_Text 재질 Outline Width, Outline Color, Face Dilate, Underlay Color TMP_Text 글자별 Char Scale, Char Position, Char Rotation, Char Color, Char Alpha 2D, 3D, 카메라, 소리 대상 트랙 SpriteRenderer Color, Alpha Renderer (MeshRenderer 등) Material 트랙: 재질의 색, 숫자, 벡터 속성마다 하나 (예: Material _BaseColor) Light Light Color, Intensity, Range (Point, Spot), Spot Angle (Spot) Camera Camera Background, Camera Size, Field of View, Near Clip, Far Clip, Viewport Rect AudioSource Volume, Pitch 이벤트와 사운드 대상 트랙 루트 Animation Events, Sound 그 밖의 트랙 UIEffect를 설치하면 UIEffect 트랙 14종이 추가됩니다. 자세한 내용은 연동을 참고하세요. 프로젝트의 컴포넌트를 움직이는 트랙은 직접 만들 수 있습니다. 자세한 내용은 커스텀 트랙 만들기를 참고하세요. 알아 둘 점 Group Alpha는 화면이나 팝업 전체를 페이드할 때 씁니다. Rotation과 World Rotation은 오일러 각(도)입니다. 값을 −180~180 범위로 읽으므로, −30°에서 0°로 갈 때 먼 쪽으로 돌지 않습니다. Active는 키 사이를 보간하지 않고, 키 시간에 오브젝트를 켜거나 끕니다. Material 트랙은 MaterialPropertyBlock으로 씁니다. 재질 에셋은 바뀌지 않고, 같은 재질을 쓰는 다른 오브젝트에도 영향을 주지 않습니다. TMP 재질 트랙은 그 텍스트만 쓰는 재질 인스턴스를 만듭니다. 미리보기를 멈추면 원래 재질로 돌아옵니다. 트랙 대상 바꾸기 트랙의 대상을 바꾸려면 트랙 인스펙터 맨 위의 경로 · 속성 ▾ 버튼을 누릅니다.

articles/ko/animation-events.html.title: 애니메이션 이벤트 | KeyTween
articles/ko/animation-events.html.summary: 애니메이션 이벤트 에디터의 이벤트 트랙에 놓은 이벤트를 코드에서 받는 방법입니다. 재생이 이벤트의 시간을 지나면 이벤트가 발생합니다. 이벤트 데이터 형식 만들기 struct에 [KeyTweenEvent]를 붙이면 에디터의 이벤트 형식 목록에 나옵니다. [KeyTweenEvent("Popup Sound")] public struct PopupSoundEvent { public string clip; public float volume; } public 필드는 JSON으로 저장됩니다. 오브젝트 참조는 저장할 수 없습니다. 형식 목록에는 플레이어 빌드에 포함되는 struct만 나옵니다. 모든 이벤트 받기 event KeyTweenEventHandler EventRaised는 재생이 이벤트를 지날 때 발생합니다. Complete는 건너뛴 이벤트를 순서대로 발생시키고, 취소는 이벤트를 발생시키지 않습니다. anim.EventRaised += (in KeyTweenEventInfo e) => Debug.Log($"{e.State}:{e.Name} @ {e.Time}"); 데이터 형식별로 받기 AddListener<T>는 데이터 형식이 T인 이벤트만 받습니다. 돌려받은 IDisposable의 Dispose로 해제합니다. using var sub = anim.AddListener<PopupSoundEvent>((in KeyTweenEventInfo e, in PopupSoundEvent data) => Play(data.clip)); 이벤트 기다리기 WaitEventAsync는 어느 상태에서든 그 이름의 이벤트가 다음에 발생하면 완료됩니다. 결과는 Awaitable<KeyTweenEventInfo>입니다. var info = await anim.WaitEventAsync("Shown"); 이벤트 정보 읽기 KeyTweenEventInfo는 readonly struct이며, in으로 전달됩니다. 다음 멤버를 제공합니다. 멤버 형식 내용 Animation KeyTween 이벤트를 낸 KeyTween State string 재생 중이던 상태 이름 Name string 이벤트 이름 Time float 상태 안에서 이벤트의 시간(초) TryGetData<T>(out T) bool 이벤트 데이터가 T이면 꺼내고 true 이벤트 하나를 여러 데이터 형식 중 하나로 처리할 때 TryGetData를 씁니다. anim.EventRaised += (in KeyTweenEventInfo e) => { if (e.TryGetData(out PopupSoundEvent sound)) audio.PlayOneShot(Load(sound.clip), sound.volume); else if (e.Name == "Shown") EnableInput(); }; 코드 없이 받기 KeyTweenEventListener 컴포넌트로 코드 없이 이벤트를 받을 수 있습니다. Add Component > KeyTween > Event Listener를 추가합니다. 이벤트 이름에 UnityEvent를 연결합니다. 이때 이벤트 데이터는 넘어가지 않습니다.

articles/ko/arrival.html.title: 도착 방식 | KeyTween
articles/ko/arrival.html.summary: 도착 방식 키는 언제(시간) 어떤 값이 될지만 정합니다. 두 키 사이를 어떻게 지나갈지는 도착 방식(Arrival)이 정합니다. 서랍을 열 때 처음에는 빠르게 당기다가 끝에서 천천히 멈추는 것처럼, 같은 거리를 같은 시간에 움직여도 속도가 어떻게 바뀌느냐에 따라 느낌이 완전히 달라집니다. 위 그래프의 세 선은 키가 같습니다. 0초에 0, 끝에 1입니다. 다른 것은 Arrival뿐입니다. 키마다 하나, 들어오는 구간에 Arrival은 키마다 하나씩 있고, 이전 키에서 이 키로 들어오는 구간의 움직임을 정합니다. 키가 셋이면 구간이 둘이고, 구간마다 다른 Arrival을 쓸 수 있습니다. 키 1 → 키 2 구간은 키 2의 Arrival로, 키 2 → 키 3 구간은 키 3의 Arrival로 움직입니다. 첫 키는 들어오는 구간이 없으므로 Arrival이 비활성입니다. 단, Start가 Current Value이고 키가 하나뿐이면, 재생할 때의 값에서 그 키로 들어오는 구간에 그 키의 Arrival을 씁니다. 에디터에서 고르기 타임라인에서 키를 고릅니다. 키 인스펙터의 Arrival 섹션에서 Type을 고릅니다. Type에 맞는 칸을 정합니다. 아래 그래프가 바로 바뀌어, 이전 키의 값(아래 선)에서 이 키의 값(위 선)까지 어떻게 지나가는지 보여 줍니다. Type 정하는 칸 이럴 때 Ease Ease (곡선 36종) 대부분의 연출. 정해진 곡선에서 고릅니다 Curve Animation Curve 원하는 모양이 Ease에 없을 때 직접 그립니다 Punch Ease, Frequency, Damping 톡 튀었다가 제자리로 돌아오는 반응 Shake Ease, Frequency, Damping 무작위로 떨렸다가 제자리로 돌아오는 반응 키를 여러 개 고르면 Arrival 섹션만 나오고, 고른 키를 한꺼번에 바꿉니다. 키마다 값이 다른 칸은 —로 보입니다. 결과는 ▶ 미리보기로 바로 확인합니다. Ease: 정해진 곡선 고르기 가장 많이 쓰는 Type입니다. 곡선 36종 중 하나를 고릅니다. 이름의 두 부분이 각각 다음을 뜻합니다. 부분 뜻 In / Out / InOut 어디가 느린지. In은 출발이 느리고 점점 빨라집니다. Out은 빠르게 출발해 도착이 느립니다. InOut은 양쪽이 느립니다 Sine → Quad → Cubic → Quart → Quint → Expo 변화의 세기. 오른쪽으로 갈수록 느린 부분과 빠른 부분의 차이가 커집니다 Circ 원호 모양 Back 출발 전에 살짝 뒤로 가거나(In), 목표를 살짝 지나쳤다가(Out) 돌아옵니다 Elastic 고무줄처럼 출렁입니다 Bounce 바닥에 튀듯이 도착합니다 Linear부터 InOutBounce까지 앞의 32종은 LitMotion Ease와 번호와 공식이 같습니다. OutBackQuad부터 OutBackQuint까지는 Unity-AnimationUI의 OutBack 계열입니다. 뒤로 갈수록 더 크게 지나쳤다가 돌아옵니다. CustomAnimationCurve는 Ease로 고르면 Linear와 같습니다. 곡선을 직접 그리려면 Type을 Curve로 고릅니다. UI에서 고르는 요령 정답은 없지만, 다음에서 시작하면 대부분 자연스럽습니다. 연출 먼저 써 볼 Ease 이유 화면에 들어오기, 팝업 열기 OutCubic, OutQuart 빠르게 나타나고 부드럽게 멈춰서 반응이 빠르게 느껴집니다 화면에서 나가기, 닫기 InCubic, InQuad 천천히 출발해 빠르게 사라져서 사라지는 장면을 오래 보여 주지 않습니다 한 자리에서 다른 자리로 (탭 전환, 슬라이드) InOutSine, InOutCubic 출발과 도착이 모두 부드럽습니다 버튼을 누른 반응, 튀어나오는 팝업 OutBack 살짝 지나쳤다가 돌아와서 탄력이 느껴집니다 떨어져서 착지 OutBounce 바닥에 튀는 모습이 그대로 납니다 숫자 세기, 진행 바 Linear, OutQuad 일정한 속도이거나 끝에서만 살짝 느려집니다 반복하는 숨쉬기, 맥박 (Loop) InOutSine 끝과 처음이 같은 속도(0)라서 바퀴 사이가 끊기지 않습니다 Curve: 곡선을 직접 그리기 원하는 모양이 Ease에 없으면 Type을 Curve로 고르고 Animation Curve 칸을 눌러 Unity의 곡선 편집기에서 직접 그립니다. 가로는 구간의 진행입니다. 0이 이전 키의 시간, 1이 이 키의 시간입니다. 세로는 값입니다. 0이 이전 키의 값, 1이 이 키의 값입니다. 1을 넘거나 0보다 작으면 목표를 지나치거나 반대쪽으로 갔다가 돌아옵니다. 끝점은 보통 (1, 1)에 둡니다. 그래야 이 키의 시간에 이 키의 값에 정확히 닿습니다. Punch와 Shake: 흔들고 제자리로 버튼을 눌렀을 때 톡 튀는 반응이나, 오류가 났을 때 떨리는 연출에 씁니다. 다른 Type과 달리 **이 키의 값은 목적지가 아니라 흔들림의 세기(Strength)**입니다. 값은 이전 키의 값을 중심으로 흔들리다가, 구간이 끝나면 이전 키의 값으로 돌아옵니다. Punch는 정해진 박자로 왕복합니다. Shake는 축마다 매 프레임 무작위로 흔들립니다. 칸 뜻 새 키의 값 Strength (키의 값) 흔들림의 크기. 축마다 따로 정합니다. 위 예는 Z축으로 15도까지 흔들립니다 — Frequency 흔들리는 빠르기. 클수록 자주 흔들립니다. LitMotion의 frequency와 같은 값입니다 10 Damping 흔들림이 잦아드는 정도. 1이면 끝으로 갈수록 잦아들고, 0이면 끝까지 같은 세기로 흔들리다가 제자리로 돌아옵니다 1 Ease 흔들림을 시간에 어떻게 펼칠지. Out Sine이면 흔들림이 앞쪽에 몰리고 뒤로 갈수록 느려집니다 Out Sine 공식은 LitMotion의 LMotion.Punch, LMotion.Shake와 같습니다. 끝나면 제자리로 돌아오므로 Punch 키는 보통 "제자리 키 다음"에 둡니다. 예를 들어 0초 키(Scale 1) 다음에 0.3초 Punch 키(Strength 0.2)를 두면, 크기 1을 중심으로 톡 튀었다가 1로 돌아옵니다. 코드에서 바꾸기 재생할 때마다 도착 방식을 바꾸려면 With를 씁니다. 바꾼 값은 그 재생에만 적용되고, 끝나면 에디터에서 정한 값으로 돌아옵니다. 바꾸는 것은 그 트랙의 마지막 키(끝 값에 도착하는 구간)입니다. anim.With("Open").WithEase(panel, KeyTweenProperty.Scale, KeyTweenEase.OutBack).Play(); anim.With("Hit").WithShake(icon, KeyTweenProperty.AnchoredPosition, frequency: 20f, damping: 0.5f).Play(); 코드로 상태를 만들 때는 Key(time, value, ease), KeyCurve, KeyPunch, KeyShake로 키마다 정합니다. 자세한 내용은 API를 참고하세요. 알아 둘 점 Start가 Current Value인 트랙은 첫 구간이 재생할 때의 값에서 출발합니다. 도착 방식은 같게 적용됩니다. Active처럼 켜고 끄는 트랙에는 중간값이 없습니다. 키의 시간에 바로 바뀝니다. 재생 중에는 Ease만 쓰는 트랙을 Burst로 한꺼번에 계산합니다. Curve, Punch, Shake 키가 있는 트랙은 일반 코드로 계산합니다. 동시에 수백 개를 재생할 때만 차이가 납니다. 자세한 내용은 성능을 참고하세요.

articles/ko/awaiting-several.html.title: 여러 KeyTween 함께 기다리기 | KeyTween
articles/ko/awaiting-several.html.summary: 여러 KeyTween 함께 기다리기 여러 오브젝트의 KeyTween을 동시에 재생하고, 모두 끝날 때까지 기다리는 방법입니다. 모두 시작한 뒤 차례로 기다리기 PlayAsync는 .NET Task가 아니라 Unity Awaitable을 돌려주므로 Task.WhenAll에 바로 넣을 수 없습니다. 대신 재생은 PlayAsync를 부르는 순간 시작됩니다. 전부 먼저 시작해 두고 차례로 기다리면 WhenAll과 같은 결과를 얻습니다. var plays = anims.Select(a => a.PlayAsync("Hover")).ToList(); // 여기서 모두 동시에 시작합니다 foreach (var play in plays) await play; // 모두 끝날 때까지 기다립니다 Task.WhenAll로 기다리기 Task.WhenAll을 쓰려면 각 재생을 Task로 감쌉니다. static async Task AsTask(Awaitable awaitable) => await awaitable; await Task.WhenAll(anims.Select(a => AsTask(a.PlayAsync("Hover")))); UniTask.WhenAll로 기다리기 UniTask를 설치했다면 연동에서 제공하는 PlayUniTaskAsync를 쓸 수 있습니다. await UniTask.WhenAll(anims.Select(a => a.PlayUniTaskAsync("Hover"))); 하나가 취소되면 재생 중 하나라도 취소되면(끝나는 경우) OperationCanceledException이 발생합니다. 예외가 발생하는 위치는 방법마다 다릅니다. 차례로 기다리기: 취소된 재생을 기다리는 await Task.WhenAll, UniTask.WhenAll: WhenAll

articles/ko/build.html.title: 코드로 상태 만들기 | KeyTween
articles/ko/build.html.summary: 코드로 상태 만들기 상태는 보통 에디터에서 만들지만, 코드만으로 만들 수도 있습니다. 대상이 실행 중에야 정해지는 연출이나, 에디터를 쓰지 않는 작은 연출에 씁니다. Build(state)로 트랙과 키를 쌓고, Add로 추가하거나 Play 계열로 추가와 재생을 함께 합니다. anim.Build("Pop") .Track(button.transform, KeyTweenProperty.Scale) // 트랙 시작. 다음 Track 전까지의 Key는 이 트랙에 .Key(0f, Vector3.one) .Key(0.15f, Vector3.one * 1.2f, KeyTweenEase.OutBack) // 이 키로 오는 구간을 OutBack으로 .Key(0.3f, Vector3.one, KeyTweenEase.InOutSine) .Track(label, KeyTweenProperty.GraphicAlpha) .Key(0f, 0f).Key(0.2f, 1f) .Event(0.15f, "Peak") .OnComplete(() => Debug.Log("popped")) .Play(); 메서드 하는 일 Track(target, property) 내장 속성의 트랙을 시작합니다. Material 트랙은 Track(renderer, "_BaseColor"), 커스텀 트랙은 Track<MyTrack>(target) From(start) 트랙의 Start. 기본은 KeyTweenStart.KeyValue(첫 키)이고, KeyTweenStart.Current(재생할 때의 값), KeyTweenStart.Pointer를 고를 수 있습니다 Key(time, value, ease) 키 하나. ease는 이 키로 오는 구간의 도착 방식(기본 OutSine, 에디터와 같음). 값은 Vector4나 float이고 Vector3, Vector2, Color도 넘길 수 있습니다 KeyCurve(time, value, curve), KeyPunch(time, strength, frequency = 10, damping = 1), KeyShake(...) 도착 방식이 Curve, Punch, Shake인 키. 값은 Vector4(Vector3, Vector2, Color도 됨)이고, Punch와 Shake의 값은 도착할 곳이 아니라 흔들리는 세기입니다 Event(time, name), Sound(time, clip, volume) 애니메이션 이벤트와 사운드 Loop() 반복 상태로 OnStart, OnComplete, OnCancel 상태의 콜백 (이 상태의 모든 재생) Add() 상태를 추가합니다. 이후 anim.Play("Pop")처럼 이름으로 재생합니다 Play(), PlayAsync(), PlayReversed(), PlayReversedAsync() 추가하고 재생합니다 With() 추가하고, 재생 설정(With)으로 이어 갑니다 만든 상태는 실행 중에만 있는 상태입니다. 저장되지 않고, 에디터에서 만든 상태와 똑같이 Play, Stop, Complete, With를 쓸 수 있습니다. 키는 넣은 순서와 상관없이 시간 순서로 놓입니다. 같은 이름의 상태가 있으면 바꿉니다. 그 상태가 재생 중이면 멈추고, 기다리던 PlayAsync는 취소됩니다. Track 없이 Key를 부르면 바로 예외가 납니다. 상태 객체로 추가하기 KeyTweenState를 직접 만들어 AddState로 넣을 수도 있습니다. Build는 내부에서 이 메서드를 씁니다. 화면 전환 컨테이너가 기본 전환 연출을 넣을 때도 씁니다(Screens). public void AddState(KeyTweenState state); 이미 만들어진 상태 객체를 받는 곳에 씁니다. 예를 들어 기본 전환 연출을 이름을 붙여 다른 화면에도 넣을 수 있습니다. var fade = KeyTweenDefaultTransitions.FadeIn(screen); fade.name = "FadeIn"; screen.Animation.AddState(fade); screen.Animation.Play("FadeIn"); 같은 이름의 상태가 있으면 바꿉니다. 그 상태가 재생 중이면 멈추고 On Cancel을 부릅니다. 다른 KeyTween의 상태를 바탕으로 만들 때는 state.Clone()으로 복사본을 넣습니다. 같은 객체를 두 곳에 넣으면 한쪽에서 고친 것이 다른 쪽에도 바뀝니다. 복사본의 트랙도 원래 대상(Component)을 그대로 가리킵니다.

articles/ko/comparison.html.summary: 다른 도구와 비교 이 페이지는 같은 연출을 도구마다 어떤 절차로 만드는지 비교합니다. 비교 내용은 모두 이 저장소에서 실제로 만들어 본 결과를 근거로 합니다. Benchmarks/Assets/Bench/*Driver.cs: 맥박, 목록 등장, 글자 물결의 세 가지 연출을 방식별로 구현한 코드 Assets/Reference: Unity-AnimationUI와 UnityScreenNavigator의 데모를 재현한 것 Assets/KeyTween/Samples/RPG: RPG 샘플 다른 도구는 이 작업에서 직접 써 본 범위만 적었습니다. 써 보지 않은 기능은 "확인 안 함"으로 표시했습니다. 성능 비교는 성능 페이지에서 따로 다룹니다. 1. 한 연출을 만드는 절차 — 버튼 맥박 (크기 + 색, 반복) 버튼의 크기와 색이 반복해서 바뀌는 맥박 연출을 예로 들어, 도구별 제작 절차와 실행에 필요한 코드를 비교합니다. 한눈에 보기 도구 만드는 곳 실행 코드 KeyTween KeyTween 창 0줄 (코드로 부를 때 1줄) Animator Animation 창 + Animator 창 0줄 (기본 상태) DOTween Pro 인스펙터(DOTweenAnimation) 또는 코드 2줄 LitMotion 코드 2개 문장(4줄) AnimationUI 인스펙터(AnimationUI 시퀀스 목록) 반복하려면 1줄 KeyTween으로 만들기 KeyTween 창에서 만듭니다. 버튼에 KeyTween을 추가합니다. 상태 "Pulse"를 만들고 Loop를 켭니다. 트랙 추가 창에서 Scale과 Color를 고릅니다. 0 / 0.5 / 1초에 키를 두고, 이징을 InOutSine으로 합니다. Play On을 OnEnable로 둡니다. 켜질 때 재생되므로 실행 코드는 0줄입니다. 코드로 부를 때는 1줄이면 됩니다. anim.Play("Pulse"); KeyTween의 상태, 트랙, 키 위 절차에 나온 세 가지 개념입니다. 상태: 이름이 붙은 연출 하나 트랙: 상태 안에서 크기나 색 같은 값 하나를 바꾸는 줄 키: 트랙 위에서 특정 시점의 값 상태 만들기, 트랙 추가, 키 편집은 모두 아래의 KeyTween 창에서 처리합니다. Animator로 만들기 Animation 창과 Animator 창에서 만듭니다. Animation 창에서 Create를 누릅니다. 클립과 컨트롤러 에셋 2개가 생깁니다. Record로 키를 찍습니다. 클립의 Loop Time을 확인합니다. 컨트롤러에서 기본 상태를 확인합니다. 기본 상태로 재생되므로 실행 코드는 0줄입니다. 다른 연출로 바꾸려면 상태와 전환을 쓰거나 Play를 부릅니다. DOTween Pro로 만들기 인스펙터(DOTweenAnimation) 또는 코드로 만듭니다. 인스펙터: 효과 하나당 컴포넌트 하나를 붙입니다(크기 1개 + 색 1개). Loops는 −1, Yoyo로 둡니다. 코드: 아래 2줄입니다. DOScale(...).SetLoops(-1, Yoyo) DOColor(...)... LitMotion으로 만들기 코드로만 만듭니다. 값마다 Motion 하나를 만들고 대상에 바인딩하며, 맥박 전체는 2개 문장, 4줄입니다. 그중 크기 쪽은 다음과 같습니다. LMotion.Create(...).WithLoops(-1, Yoyo).BindToLocalScale(rt) AnimationUI로 만들기 인스펙터의 AnimationUI 시퀀스 목록에 단계를 넣습니다. 크기·색 단계 Wait 되돌리는 단계 Wait 반복 기능이 없으므로, 반복하려면 코드 1줄이 필요합니다. OnAnimationEnded += Play 2. 연출별로 드는 일 측정 프로젝트에서는 모든 방식을 같은 조건에서 재기 위해 전부 코드로 구현했습니다. 하지만 실제로 쓸 때 중요한 차이는 연출을 에디터에서 만들 수 있는지입니다. 연출마다 만드는 곳 연출마다 각 도구에서 어디서, 어떻게 만드는지 정리했습니다. 연출 KeyTween Animator
